newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan state firms July-Feb profits fall short.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan state firms July-Feb profits fall short.

text.p: The big eight state firms run by Taiwan's economics ministry reported combined pre-tax profits of T$42.773 billion for July 1996-February 1997, failing to reach a T$47.773 billion target, the ministry said on Thursday.
Taiwan Power Co led the profit gains, earning T$39.455 billion, followed by Taiwan Salt Works with a profit of T$4.168 billion, the ministry said in a statement.

Taiwan Sugar Corp reported a pre-tax profit of T$782 million, Aerospace Industrial Development Corp earned T$745 million, Taiwan Fertiliser Co earned T$142 million and China Shipbuilding Corp earned T$107 million.
But firms that suffered losses were Chinese Petroleum Corp, with T$1.965 billion in pre-tax red ink, and Taiwan Manufacturing Corp, which lost T$661 million.
The ministry attributed Chinese Petroleum's loss to high oil prices, which pushed average crude import costs to US$20.78 per barrel compared to a budgeted US$15.26.
Chinese Petroleum, based on the budgeted import oil price of US$15.26 per barrel, had planned a pre-tax profit of T$12.805 billion in the July-February period, the ministry said.
